extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of public water systems, state primacy agencies, and drinking water compliance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for enhanced filtration and disinfection for public water systems (primarily systems serving ≥10,000 people) and the public notification (tiered) requirements for drinking water violations and other situations. Includes monitoring, profiling, benchmarking, filtration performance, reporting, recordkeeping, and timelines for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Subpart P (general requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of this subpart P constitute national primary drinking water regulations. These regulations establish requirements for filtration and disinfection that are in addition to criteria under which filtration and disinfection are required under subpart H of this part. The requirements of this subpart are applicable to subpart H systems serving at least 10,000 people, beginning January 1, 2002 unless otherwise specified in this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment technique requirements consist of installing and properly operating water treatment processes which reliably achieve specified pathogen removal/inactivation (e.g., at least 99 percent (2-log) removal of Cryptosporidium for filtered systems or equivalent watershed control for unfiltered systems) and compliance with profiling and benchmarking (§ 141.172).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment technique requirement for Cryptosporidium (filtered systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 99 percent (2-log) removal of Cryptosporidium between a point where the raw water is not subject to recontamination by surface water runoff and a point downstream before or at the first customer for filtered systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment processes must be installed and properly operated to reliably achieve this removal. Alternative/combined segment calculations allowed per profiling procedures (§ 141.172(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptosporidium control for unfiltered systems (watershed control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cryptosporidium control under the watershed control plan for unfiltered systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems avoiding filtration must maintain a watershed control program to minimize potential for contamination by Cryptosporidium oocysts (see § 141.171).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance pathways for Subpart P requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system subject to this subpart is in compliance if: (1) it meets the requirements for avoiding filtration in §§ 141.71 and 141.171 and the disinfection requirements in §§ 141.72 and 141.172; or (2) it meets the applicable filtration requirements in either § 141.73 or § 141.173 and the disinfection requirements in §§ 141.72 and 141.172.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must select and meet either the avoiding-filtration pathway (including watershed controls and disinfection profiling) or the filtration + disinfection pathway as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on uncovered finished water storage construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems are not permitted to begin construction of uncovered finished water storage facilities beginning February 16, 1999.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation for systems that grow above 10,000 population
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H systems that did not conduct optional monitoring under § 141.172 because they served fewer than 10,000 persons when such monitoring was required, but serve more than 10,000 persons prior to January 1, 2005 must comply with §§ 141.170, 141.171, 141.173, 141.174, and 141.175 and consult with the State to establish a disinfection benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system that decides to make a significant change to its disinfection practice must consult with the State prior to making such change (see § 141.172(c)(1)(i)-(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Watershed control program requirements for avoiding filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must maintain the watershed control program under § 141.71(b)(2) to minimize the potential for contamination by Cryptosporidium oocysts in the source water. The watershed control program must: (1) identify watershed characteristics and activities which may have an adverse effect on source water quality; and (2) monitor the occurrence of activities which may have an adverse effect on source water quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These site-specific conditions are in addition to § 141.71(b) requirements; monitoring and identification must be tailored to Cryptosporidium risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: State onsite inspection adequacy criteria for avoiding filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: During the onsite inspection conducted under § 141.71(b)(3), the State must determine whether the watershed control program is adequate to limit potential contamination by Cryptosporidium oocysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequacy must be based on: comprehensiveness of the watershed review; effectiveness of the system's program to monitor and control detrimental activities; and extent to which the water system has maximized land ownership and/or controlled land use within the watershed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of systems required to profile (TTHM/HAA5 annual averages)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system must determine its TTHM annual average and its HAA5 annual average using specified procedures. The annual average is the arithmetic average of the quarterly averages of four consecutive quarters of monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for which data sets to use: systems with subpart M data use last four quarters under § 141.142; systems using grandfathered HAA5 data or other allowed datasets must use TTHM/HAA5 data collected at the same time under §§ 141.12 and 141.30; deadlines and options for systems without four quarters of HAA5 data are provided (monitoring by March 16, 1999 and determinations by March 31, 2000 or electing to comply as if monitoring had shown threshold exceedance). States may approve more representative annual datasets or require them. Systems must submit data on specified schedules. Any system with TTHM annual average ≥0.064 mg/L or HAA5 annual average ≥0.048 mg/L during the identified period must comply with profiling and benchmarking provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection profiling requirement (when triggered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system that meets the criteria (e.g., TTHM ≥0.064 mg/L or HAA5 ≥0.048 mg/L) must develop a disinfection profile of its disinfection practice for a period of up to three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system must monitor daily for a period of 12 consecutive calendar months to determine total logs of inactivation for each day of operation based on CT99.9 values in § 141.74(b) through the entire treatment plant; monitoring must begin by the specified date (not later than April 1, 2000 in original rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection profiling monitoring parameters and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: To develop the disinfection profile the system must monitor parameters necessary to determine the total inactivation ratio using analytical methods in § 141.74(a): (i) temperature of disinfected water once per day at each residual disinfectant sampling point during peak hourly flow; (ii) if chlorine is used, pH once per day at each chlorine residual sampling point during peak hourly flow; (iii) disinfectant contact time(s) (T) determined for each day during peak hourly flow; (iv) residual disinfectant concentration(s) (C) measured each day during peak hourly flow at points before/at first customer and prior to each additional disinfectant application point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems with more than one point of disinfectant application must conduct monitoring for each disinfection segment. Analytical methods per § 141.74(a) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative to daily profiling monitoring (use of existing operational data)
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of the monitoring under (b)(2), a PWS that has three years of existing operational data may submit those data, a profile generated using those data, and a request that the State approve use of those data in lieu of monitoring. The State must determine whether these operational data are substantially equivalent and representative of Giardia inactivation through the entire plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until State approval, the system must conduct the required daily monitoring. Existing data may also be used to develop additional yearly profiles and benchmarks subject to State approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total inactivation ratio and conversion to logs
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system uses only one point of disinfectant application, it may determine the total inactivation ratio either by (A) one inactivation ratio (CTcalc/CT99.9) before or at the first customer during peak flow, or (B) successive CTcalc/CT99.9 values for sequences between point of application and first customer summed to determine Σ(CTcalc/CT99.9). If multiple disinfectant points exist, determine the CT for each disinfection segment and calculate (CTcalc/CT99.9) for each and Σ(CTcalc/CT99.9). The total logs of inactivation is obtained by multiplying the value by 3.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems using chloramines or ozone for primary disinfection must also calculate logs of inactivation for viruses using a State-approved method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of disinfection profile data
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must retain disinfection profile data in graphic form, as a spreadsheet, or in some other format acceptable to the State for review as part of sanitary surveys conducted by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection benchmarking and consultation for significant changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system required to develop a disinfection profile that decides to make a significant change to its disinfection practice must consult with the State prior to making such change. Significant changes include: changes to the point of disinfection; changes to the disinfectant(s) used; changes to the disinfection process; and any other modification identified by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system modifying disinfection practice must calculate its disinfection benchmark per specified procedure and submit description of the proposed change, the disinfection profile and benchmark, and analysis of how the proposed change will affect current disinfection levels to the State as part of consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of disinfection benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: For each year of profiling data, determine the lowest average monthly Giardia inactivation. The disinfection benchmark is the lowest monthly average value (for one year of data) or the average of lowest monthly average values (for more than one year of data) of the monthly logs of Giardia inactivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems using chloramines or ozone must also calculate the disinfection benchmark for viruses using a State-approved method. The benchmark and supporting profile/analysis must be submitted during State consultation for proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration requirement for systems not qualifying to avoid filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system subject to this subpart that does not meet all criteria for avoiding filtration must provide treatment consisting of both disinfection (as in § 141.72(b)) and filtration treatment which complies with § 141.173(a) or (b) or § 141.73(b) or (c) by December 31, 2001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filtration requirement is in addition to disinfection; systems must choose approved filtration technology or obtain State approval for alternative technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventional/direct filtration turbidity performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems using conventional filtration or direct filtration: (1) the turbidity level of representative samples of a system's filtered water must be ≤ 0.3 NTU in at least 95 percent of the measurements taken each month; (2) the turbidity level must at no time exceed 1 NTU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement procedures specified in § 141.74(a) and (c). Systems using lime softening may acidify samples prior to analysis with a State-approved protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criteria for alternative filtration technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system may use a filtration technology not listed if it demonstrates to the State, using pilot plant studies or other means, that the alternative technology, combined with disinfection meeting § 141.72(b), consistently achieves 99.9 percent removal/inactivation of Giardia cysts and 99.99 percent removal/inactivation of viruses, and 99 percent removal of Cryptosporidium oocysts, and the State approves the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each approval, the State will set turbidity performance requirements the system must meet at least 95 percent of the time and which the system may not exceed at any time, such that the performance consistently achieves the specified removal/inactivation percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous turbidity monitoring for filtration systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems providing conventional filtration or direct filtration must conduct continuous monitoring of turbidity for each individual filter using an approved method in § 141.74(a) and must calibrate turbidimeters per manufacturer procedure. Systems must record individual filter monitoring results every 15 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuous monitoring equipment fails, the system must conduct grab sampling every four hours in lieu of continuous monitoring for no more than five working days following equipment failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly turbidity reporting to State
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems subject to this subpart that provide conventional filtration or direct filtration must report monthly to the State turbidity measurements as required by § 141.173 within 10 days after the end of each month the system serves water to the public. Required information includes: (1) total number of filtered water turbidity measurements taken during the month; (2) number and percentage of measurements ≤ turbidity limits specified; (3) date and value of any turbidity measurements >1 NTU (or >State maximum for alternative technologies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting in § 141.175(a) is in lieu of reporting specified in § 141.75(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of individual filter monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must maintain results of individual filter monitoring taken under § 141.174 for at least three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must also report that they have conducted individual filter turbidity monitoring within 10 days after the end of each month the system serves water to the public, and report specific individual filter measurement results only if certain exceedance conditions are met (see subsequent criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and actions for individual filter turbidity exceedance (>1.0 NTU two consecutive readings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any individual filter that has a measured turbidity > 1.0 NTU in two consecutive measurements taken 15 minutes apart, the system must report the filter number, the turbidity measurement, and the date(s) of the exceedance. In addition, the system must either produce a filter profile within 7 days of the exceedance (if no obvious reason is identified) and report that the profile has been produced or report the obvious reason for the exceedance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and actions for turbidity >0.5 NTU after backwash (two consecutive readings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any individual filter that has a measured turbidity > 0.5 NTU in two consecutive measurements taken 15 minutes apart at the end of the first four hours of continuous filter operation after backwashing or being taken offline, the system must report the filter number, turbidity, and date(s). In addition, the system must either produce a filter profile within 7 days of the exceedance (if no obvious reason) and report it or report the obvious reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment requirement for recurrent >1.0 NTU exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: For any individual filter that has a measured turbidity > 1.0 NTU in two consecutive measurements taken 15 minutes apart at any time in each of three consecutive months, the system must report the filter number, measurement, and dates, and must conduct a self-assessment of the filter within 14 days of the exceedance and report that the self-assessment was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The self-assessment must consist of: assessment of filter performance; development of a filter profile; identification and prioritization of factors limiting filter performance; assessment of the applicability of corrections; and preparation of a filter self-assessment report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive performance evaluation trigger and timeline (>2.0 NTU recurrent exceedances)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any individual filter that has a measured turbidity > 2.0 NTU in two consecutive measurements taken 15 minutes apart at any time in each of two consecutive months, the system must report the filter number, measurement, and dates, arrange for a comprehensive performance evaluation by the State or a State-approved third party no later than 30 days following the exceedance, and have the evaluation completed and submitted to the State no later than 90 days following the exceedance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate notification to State for certain turbidity exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: If at any time the turbidity exceeds 1 NTU in representative samples of filtered water in a conventional/direct filtration system, the system must inform the State as soon as possible, but no later than the end of the next business day. Similarly, if turbidity exceeds the State-set maximum for alternative technologies, the system must inform the State as soon as possible, but no later than the end of the next business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must give public notice (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner or operator of a public water system (community, non-transient non-community, and transient non-community systems) must give notice for all violations of national primary drinking water regulations (NPDWR) and for other situations listed in Table 1. 'NPDWR violations' includes violations of MCL, MRDL, treatment technique (TT), monitoring requirements, and testing procedures in part 141. Appendix A identifies tier assignments for specific violations/situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primacy agency is EPA or State or Tribe exercising primary enforcement responsibility; compliance dates specified (varies by primacy/implementation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of violations and situations requiring public notice (Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations requiring public notice include: (1) NPDWR violations (failure to comply with applicable MCL/MRDL, failure to comply with TT, failure to perform required monitoring, failure to comply with testing procedures); (2) Variance and exemptions (operation under variance/exemption or failure to comply with schedule requirements); (3) Special public notices (waterborne disease outbreak/emergency; exceedance of nitrate MCL by NCWS with permission; exceedance of SMCL for fluoride; availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring data; other situations determined by primacy agency; exceedance of lead action level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A assigns tiers for each specific violation/situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier definitions for public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice requirements are divided into three tiers based on seriousness: Tier 1 required for NPDWR violations and situations with significant potential to have serious adverse effects on human health as a result of short-term exposure; Tier 2 required for all other NPDWR violations and situations with potential to have serious adverse health effects; Tier 3 required for all other NPDWR violations and situations not included in Tier 1 or Tier 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A identifies tier assignment for each specific violation/situation; tier determines form, manner, and frequency of notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must be notified and distribution limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public water system must provide public notice to persons served. Systems that sell/provide water to consecutive systems must give notice to the owner/operator of the consecutive system, and the consecutive system is responsible for notifying its persons served. If a violation is limited to a physically/hydraulically isolated portion of the distribution system, the primacy agency may allow limiting notice distribution to only persons served by that portion if permission is granted in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the notice must also be sent to the primacy agency and the Administrator (as applicable) per § 141.31(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 notice: situations requiring Tier 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 1 required for: (1) Violation of the MCL for total coliforms when fecal coliform or E. coli are present, or failure to test for fecal/E. coli when repeat coliform sample positive; (2) Violation of MCL for nitrate/nitrite or failure to take confirmation sample within 24 hours after first exceedance; (3) Exceedance of nitrate MCL by NCWS where permitted; (4) Violation of MRDL for chlorine dioxide when distribution samples the day after an entrance exceedance exceed MRDL or required samples not taken; (5)-(6) Certain turbidity/SWTR treatment technique single exceedances where primacy agency determines Tier 1; (7) Occurrence of waterborne disease outbreak or other waterborne emergency; (8) Detection of E. coli, enterococci, or coliphage in source water samples as specified; (9) Other violations/situations with significant potential to have serious short-term health effects; (10) Exceedance of the lead action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A identifies tier assignments and may expand/clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 notice: timing, consultation, and additional steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must: (1) provide a public notice as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation/situation requiring Tier 1 notice; (2) initiate consultation with the primacy agency as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after learning of the situation to determine additional public notice requirements; (3) comply with any additional public notification requirements determined during consultation (including repeat notices, timing, form, manner, frequency, and content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 notice: form and manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must provide the Tier 1 notice within 24 hours in a form and manner reasonably calculated to reach all persons served. The form and manner must fit the specific situation and be designed to reach residential, transient, and non-transient users of the water system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primacy agency consultation can affect required form/manner and duration of posted notices; systems should choose communication methods appropriate to reach all affected customers promptly.
